paper_title: Search for Axion dark matter with the QUAX-LNF tunable haloscope
coupling_convention: |g_agamma| in GeV^-1, 90% C.L. single-sided upper limit
notes: QUAX-LNF tunable haloscope at 8.83 GHz, first run. Excludes axion DM in mass range 36.52413-36.5511 ueV with g_agamma down to 0.882e-13 GeV^-1 at 90% CL (paper body value; abstract v3 quotes 0.882, an earlier version 0.861). Only the best (minimum) limit is given numerically; the full limit curve (Fig. 7) varies up to ~1e-12 GeV^-1 across the band, so the two-point line here represents the paper's quoted best sensitivity over the scanned range. Assumes local DM density 0.45 GeV/cm^3 and standard halo model (Q_a ~ 1e6). Appendix also recasts limit as dark photon kinetic mixing chi ~1e-14 (random polarization, cos theta = 1/sqrt(3)), but the primary result is axion-photon. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.7, 60)) | Vision: Fig. 7 top panel: 90% C.L. upper limit on |g_agamma| over the previously unprobed mass window 36.5241-36.5510 ueV (3.652413e-5 to 3.65511e-5 eV). The limit curve is highly jagged (per-bin fluctuations of the power-constrained limit); traced points represent the envelope of the boundary, with typical values 1-3e-13 GeV^-1, best sensitivity 0.882e-13 GeV^-1 (quoted in text, centered at 36.53764 ueV), and steep rises at both edges of the scan. Individual spike positions are approximate due to dense fluctuation, but the overall level is calibrated by the quoted best limit and the KSVZ band (~1.5e-14, factor ~6 below the limit). Fig. 8 gives a dark-photon recast (chi ~1e-14) but the primary result is the axion-photon coupling.
